# Lecture 02.03 · 🛠 Installing Sass, Watch Mode, Source Maps, and the UI Kit Page

> **Section:** S02 · **Type:** 🛠 Build · **Track:** ★ Core · **Time:** ~30 minutes
> **Project feature:** `sass` installed; `ui-kit/index.html` (provided wireframe) styled by `styles/main.scss`

---

## 1. Goal

By the end of this lecture:

```text
taskflow/
├── package.json            ← scripts: styles:build, styles:watch
├── styles/
│   ├── main.scss           ← entry point
│   └── base/
│       └── _reset.scss     ← 📦 provided
└── ui-kit/
    ├── index.html          ← 📦 provided wireframe (unstyled at first)
    └── css/main.css        ← generated by Sass (git-ignored)
```

You'll run Sass in watch mode, edit SCSS, refresh the browser, and see changes. You'll also read the compiled CSS and the source map in DevTools.

---

## 2. Install Sass

```bash
cd /c/dev/taskflow
```

```bash
npm install -D sass
```

Check `package.json`: `sass` is now under `devDependencies`, and `package-lock.json` was created. Commit both (Lecture 01.04).

Add scripts to `package.json`:

```json
{
  "scripts": {
    "styles:build": "sass styles/main.scss ui-kit/css/main.css --style=expanded",
    "styles:watch": "sass --watch styles/main.scss ui-kit/css/main.css"
  }
}
```

Add the generated folder to `.gitignore` (it's build output):

```gitignore
# Generated UI kit CSS
ui-kit/css/
```

---

## 3. 📦 Provided: the reset

Create `styles/base/_reset.scss`:

```scss
// A small modern reset. Provided, not a learning objective.
*,
*::before,
*::after {
  box-sizing: border-box;
}

html {
  -webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%;
}

body {
  margin: 0;
  min-height: 100vh;
  line-height: 1.5;
  -webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;
}

h1, h2, h3, h4, p, ul, ol, figure {
  margin: 0;
}

ul[role='list'],
ol[role='list'] {
  list-style: none;
  padding: 0;
}

img, svg {
  display: block;
  max-width: 100%;
}

input, button, textarea, select {
  font: inherit;
  color: inherit;
}

button {
  cursor: pointer;
}
```

Why a reset? Browsers apply different default margins, font sizes and box models. A reset gives every component a predictable starting point.

## 4. 📦 Provided: the UI kit wireframe

Create `ui-kit/index.html`. It contains every component we'll style in S02–S03, with the class names we'll use (BEM-style names; explained in 03.09):

```html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8" />
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1" />
  <title>TaskFlow UI Kit</title>

</head>
<body>
  <div class="page">
    <header class="page__header">

    <main class="page__main">

        <!-- S02 knowledge check: btn--danger, btn--sm -->

        <button class="btn btn--primary btn--sm">Small</button>

      <!-- BADGES -->
      <section class="kit-section">
        <h2 class="kit-section__title">Badges</h2>
        <span class="badge badge--todo">To do</span>
        <span class="badge badge--in-progress">In progress</span>

        <span class="badge badge--priority-medium">Medium</span>
        <span class="badge badge--priority-high">High</span>
      </section>

      <!-- CARDS -->
      <section class="kit-section">
        <h2 class="kit-section__title">Task cards</h2>
        <div class="task-grid">
          <article class="card card--priority-high">
            <h3 class="card__title"><a href="#">Write quarterly report</a></h3>

            <footer class="card__meta">

            <h3 class="card__title"><a href="#">Fix login redirect bug</a></h3>
            <p class="card__body">Users land on 404 after session timeout.</p>
            <footer class="card__meta">
              <span class="badge badge--todo">To do</span>
              <span class="card__due card__due--overdue">Overdue</span>
            </footer>
          </article>
          <article class="card card--priority-low">
            <h3 class="card__title"><a href="#">Plan team offsite</a></h3>
            <p class="card__body">Shortlist three venues.</p>
            <footer class="card__meta">
              <span class="badge badge--done">Done</span>
            </footer>
          </article>
        </div>
      </section>

      <!-- FORM (Your Turn in 02.10) -->
      <section class="kit-section">
        <h2 class="kit-section__title">Form fields</h2>
        <form class="form" novalidate>
          <div class="form-field">
            <label class="form-field__label" for="title">Title</label>
            <input class="form-field__input" id="title" type="text" placeholder="What needs doing?" />
            <p class="form-field__help">Keep it short and specific.</p>
          </div>
          <div class="form-field form-field--error">
            <label class="form-field__label" for="due">Due date</label>
            <input class="form-field__input" id="due" type="date" aria-invalid="true" aria-describedby="due-error" />
            <p class="form-field__error" id="due-error">Due date cannot be in the past.</p>
          </div>
          <div class="form-field">
            <label class="form-field__label" for="priority">Priority</label>
            <select class="form-field__input" id="priority">
              <option>Low</option><option selected>Medium</option><option>High</option>

          </div>
          <div class="form-field">
            <label class="form-field__label" for="desc">Description</label>

          <div class="form__actions">
```

---

## 5. The entry file ✍️

Create `styles/main.scss`:

```scss
@use 'base/reset';

body {
  font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif;
  background: #f8fafc;
  color: #0f172a;
}
```

Notice `@use 'base/reset'`: no underscore, no `.scss`. Sass finds `base/_reset.scss` automatically. (Lecture 02.07 explains `@use` properly.)

---

## 6. Run it

```bash
npm run styles:watch
```

You should see:

```text
Compiled styles/main.scss to ui-kit/css/main.css.
Sass is watching for changes. Press Ctrl-C to stop.
```

Open `ui-kit/index.html` in your browser (double-click it, or drag it into Chrome). It looks plain, with just the reset and a font. That's expected.

Now change `background: #f8fafc;` to `background: #fef3c7;` and save. The terminal says "Compiled…". Refresh the browser. The background changes.

> 💡 Optional convenience: VS Code's **Live Server** extension (or `npx live-server ui-kit`) reloads the page automatically when `main.css` changes.

---

## 7. Look at the output and the source map

1. Open `ui-kit/css/main.css`. You'll see the reset rules followed by your `body` rule, all plain CSS. At the bottom: `/*# sourceMappingURL=main.css.map */`.
2. Open `main.css.map`. It's JSON with `sources` listing your `.scss` files and a `mappings` string (encoded line/column pairs).
3. In the browser, **F12 → Elements**, select `<body>`. In **Styles**, the rule's location says `main.scss:3` (not `main.css`). Click it and DevTools opens your SCSS source.

That link, from CSS in the browser back to your SCSS, is what the source map provides.

---

## 8. Commit

```bash
git add .
```

```bash
git commit -m "feat(styles): add sass, reset, UI kit wireframe"
```

---

## 9. Summary

- `npm install -D sass`; scripts `styles:build` and `styles:watch`.
- `styles/main.scss` is the entry point; `@use 'base/reset'` loads `_reset.scss`.
- Sass writes `ui-kit/css/main.css` (+ `.map`); the HTML links only the CSS.
- Source maps let DevTools show SCSS file/line for each rule.
